title: Space Technology & Satellite Systems
headline: Many disciplines. One mission.
intro: Turn curiosity about space into a mission you can design, model and explain. Bring mechanical design, electronics, embedded software and AI together through mission analysis, telemetry and an educational space-system demonstrator.

modules.title: Space systems foundations
modules.summary: Turn an observation need into a measurable mission.
topics: Mission lifecycle: concept, requirements, design reviews, verification and operations
Circular-orbit estimates, ground coverage and revisit as different questions
Space environment: thermal cycling, vacuum, radiation and design assumptions
Requirements, subsystem ownership and verification traceability
tools: Python / NumPy — calculations with explicit units
Jupyter — reproducible mission-analysis notebooks
Git — version mission assumptions and review evidence
modules.practice: Scope a vegetation-monitoring mission. Estimate an ideal circular-orbit period and connect three mission requirements to subsystem responsibilities.
criteria: Use orbital radius rather than altitude in the period calculation
Do not confuse orbit period with revisit time
Give each requirement a measurable verification method

modules.title: Orbit, coverage & mission analysis
modules.summary: Connect an observation objective to an explicit mission model.
topics: Orbital elements and circular-orbit approximations
Ground tracks, coverage and revisit tradeoffs
Eclipse and contact-window assumptions
Sensitivity to altitude and mission constraints
Units, reference frames and model limitations
tools: Python and NumPy — calculate and compare assumptions
Jupyter and Matplotlib — visualise orbital scenarios
GMAT or an equivalent teaching simulator — inspect a configured mission model
modules.practice: Compare two illustrative mission concepts for monitoring an area. Estimate period, examine simulated coverage and document which conclusions the simplified model cannot support.
criteria: Keep period, coverage and revisit distinct
Label units and reference-frame assumptions
Present simulator output with its configuration and limitations

modules.title: Spacecraft subsystems
modules.summary: Make the power, structure, thermal and control assumptions agree.
topics: Peak power, average demand, eclipse energy and margins
Heat-flow and structural load paths
Attitude determination versus control; pointing and stability
Voltage, timing, data-format and fault-behaviour interfaces
tools: Spreadsheet / Python — power and mass budgets
FreeCAD — conceptual mechanical envelope and interface sketches
Diagram editor — heat paths, control loops and interface records
modules.practice: Build a load table for an intermittent payload, onboard computer and radio. Explore how an eclipse or a changed payload duty cycle affects the design.
criteria: Keep watts and watt-hours distinct
Document simultaneous loads, losses and assumptions
Identify cross-subsystem effects rather than analysing each part alone

modules.title: Structures, thermal thinking & payload interfaces
modules.summary: Bring mechanical and electronics decisions into one reviewable design.
topics: Mechanical envelope, mass properties and access for assembly
Payload mounting and connector clearances
Conduction, radiation and simple thermal balances
Material choices, tolerances and environmental assumptions
Interface documentation and change control
tools: FreeCAD or equivalent CAD — model an educational assembly
Python spreadsheets or notebooks — track mass and thermal assumptions
Interface-control template — agree mechanical and electrical boundaries
modules.practice: Create a non-flight educational payload enclosure and interface drawing. Track mass, connector access and a simple thermal scenario; review a design change with another subsystem team.
deliverables: CAD concept and annotated interface drawing
criteria: Identify model simplifications and unverified loads
Show how the assembly can be connected and inspected
Do not describe the model as flight-qualified hardware

modules.title: Avionics and communications
modules.summary: Move trustworthy telemetry from a sensor model to a ground display.
topics: Sampling, scheduling, watchdogs and safe startup
Telemetry sequence numbers, timestamps, units and validity
Link budgets and useful data volume during a contact
Normal, safe and recovery states; approved commands
tools: Python — sensor, packet-loss and ground-station simulation
C/C++ with a suitable microcontroller — optional supervised bench extension
JSON / CSV — documented telemetry interchange
pytest — repeatable timeout, duplicate and recovery checks
modules.practice: Send synthetic sensor readings through a simulated link. Show missing and stale packets explicitly, and recover from a sensor timeout.
criteria: Never present missing telemetry as a real zero
Distinguish error detection from command authentication
Demonstrate a recovery path after a failed contact

modules.title: Flight-software concepts & fault management
modules.summary: Make state, timing and recovery visible in a simulated controller.
topics: Boot, nominal, safe and recovery states
Sensor sampling, command validation and telemetry queues
Watchdogs, timeout handling and resource limits
Fault detection, isolation and recovery concepts
Repeatable simulation and software verification
tools: Python state-machine simulator — explore control logic
pytest — automate fault and recovery cases
Microcontroller tooling — optional supervised ground-hardware extension
modules.practice: Build a simulated subsystem controller. Inject a missing sensor, delayed command and restart; demonstrate how the controller enters a safe state and reports the reason.
criteria: Define safe-state entry and exit conditions explicitly
Reject malformed or out-of-sequence commands
Keep recovery bounded and observable

modules.title: Ground operations, telemetry review & verification
modules.summary: Show how a team will operate and review the demonstrator.
topics: Telemetry schemas, timestamps and engineering units
Command approval, acknowledgements and stale data
Contact planning and simulated link loss
Verification matrices and acceptance evidence
Operations procedures and anomaly handover
tools: Python and Plotly — inspect replayed telemetry
CSV or SQLite — retain sample telemetry with schema metadata
Git — version procedures and verification evidence
modules.practice: Run a simulated ground-operations rehearsal. Replay a telemetry stream, lose contact, recover state and hand the next operator a clear account of what happened.
criteria: Clearly distinguish live, replayed and stale data
Trace each requirement to a test result
Keep all radio work simulated unless facilities and approvals are separately agreed

modules.title: Autonomy and mission demonstrator
modules.summary: Integrate the evidence and explain what your prototype proves.
topics: Rule-based autonomy, AI baselines and human override
Unit, integration and scenario testing
Contact plans, command approval and operations runbooks
CubeSat/CanSat-style educational mission review
tools: Python / scikit-learn — optional telemetry anomaly baseline
pytest and recorded fixtures — repeatable mission scenarios
Git and Markdown — reproducible review package and runbook
modules.practice: Integrate a mission brief, budgets and telemetry chain. Inject low energy, invalid telemetry and a missed contact; present the evidence at a guided mission review.
criteria: Compare any AI component with a simple baseline
Bound autonomous actions and define a fallback
State model limitations and unresolved risks

roles: Explore structures, packaging, materials, heat paths and physical interfaces.
Connect power, sensing, embedded interfaces and communication budgets.
Build telemetry software, ground displays, state machines and fault tests.
Investigate telemetry anomalies and observation data with measurable baselines.

projects.title: Mission concept & subsystem budget
projects.problem: A team wants to observe environmental change but has not connected the data need to a feasible mission concept.
projects.work: Create an analysis notebook and interface matrix. Mechanical and electronics students own physical assumptions; software and data students connect the payload output to a useful data product.
projects.failure: A higher-duty payload exhausts the energy allowance; a useful orbit estimate is mistaken for a revisit guarantee.
projects.evidence: A mission brief, budget workbook, tradeoff log and verification matrix.

projects.title: Ground-based telemetry demonstrator
projects.problem: A ground operator needs to understand whether received readings are fresh, valid and complete.
projects.work: Implement timestamped telemetry and a ground view. Start entirely in simulation; a supervised sensor-board extension can be scoped with the institution.
projects.failure: Duplicate packets, stale values, a reset mid-stream and missing sequence numbers must remain visible.
projects.evidence: A schema, runnable simulator, dashboard walkthrough and fault-test log.

projects.title: Integrated educational mission MVP
projects.problem: Subsystems work separately but their combined behaviour has not been reviewed.
projects.work: Combine power assumptions, telemetry and mode transitions into a CubeSat/CanSat-style mission package. Compare a simple anomaly rule with an optional ML baseline.
projects.failure: Low-energy mode, invalid sensor input and a missed contact must trigger a documented safe response.
projects.evidence: A demonstrator, test report, operations runbook and team delivery case study.
